projectDetails.trustClientName: Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust
projectDetails.projectDescription: Major refurbishment of Parkview mental health inpatient unit to create trauma-informed therapeutic environments
projectDetails.projectNarrative: Birmingham Women's and Children's NHS Foundation Trust is undertaking a comprehensive refurbishment of the Parkview mental health inpatient unit to modernise the clinical environment and create therapeutic spaces aligned with trauma-informed care principles. The existing 1970s building requires significant internal reconfiguration, new building services, and improved security features. ISG has been appointed through the ProCure23 framework with a focus on maximising off-site manufactured components to minimise disruption to adjacent operational wards and reduce the refurbishment programme duration.

revisions.description: Updated following anti-ligature product selection workshop

items.name: Minimised disruption to operational wards
items.description: Off-site fabrication of bathroom pods, wall panels, and service modules reduces noisy and disruptive on-site work duration by approximately 40%

items.name: Consistent anti-ligature detailing
items.description: Factory manufacture of anti-ligature fixtures ensures consistent safety-critical detailing that is difficult to achieve reliably with on-site installation

items.name: Improved infection control during works
items.description: Pre-assembled components reduce dust and debris generation, minimising infection risk in adjacent clinical areas

items.name: Adaptable room configurations
items.description: Demountable panel systems allow future reconfiguration of therapy rooms without major construction works

items.name: Reduced decant costs
items.description: Shorter on-site programme reduces the period and cost of decanting patients to temporary facilities

items.name: Existing building structural constraints
items.description: 1970s concrete frame limits floor-to-ceiling height available for service distribution. Existing structure requires survey to confirm load capacity for heavier MMC components.

items.name: Anti-ligature certification requirements
items.description: All fixtures and fittings in patient areas must meet anti-ligature standards. Limited range of pre-certified MMC bathroom pods available for mental health settings.

items.name: Access for component delivery
items.description: Internal refurbishment requires all components to pass through existing corridors and doorways, limiting maximum module size to 2.4m x 1.2m x 2.7m.

items.name: Has a pre-manufactured value target been set?
items.description: PMV target of 45% set, reflecting refurbishment constraints

items.name: Has a logistics strategy for MMC delivery been developed?
items.description: Detailed logistics plan developed for phased delivery through operational hospital

items.name: Is there a designated MMC coordination role on the project?
items.description: ISG pre-construction manager acting as MMC coordinator

items.name: Has a design-for-manufacture review been completed?
items.description: DfMA review completed focusing on component sizes compatible with existing building access

items.name: Percentage of building elements with standardised dimensions
items.description: 35% standardisation achieved; limited by existing building grid and varying room sizes

items.name: Have MMC suppliers been engaged in early design?
items.description: Anti-ligature bathroom pod supplier engaged at RIBA Stage 1 to inform design

items.name: Is the procurement route compatible with MMC?
items.description: ProCure23 with early contractor involvement supports MMC adoption

items.name: Percentage of packages with MMC specification included
items.description: 40% of packages include MMC specification; focused on bathrooms, wall panels, and ceiling systems

items.name: Has the client endorsed an MMC-first approach?
items.description: Trust Board supports MMC approach, particularly for patient safety benefits in anti-ligature detailing

items.name: Are clinical user groups engaged with MMC implications?
items.description: Mental health nursing team and service users involved in mock-up reviews of bathroom pod prototypes

elements.name: Structural alterations
elements.description: Localised structural modifications to accommodate new room layouts and service risers

elements.name: External wall upgrades
elements.description: New window systems with anti-ligature restrictors and external insulation overlay

elements.name: Internal walls and partitions
elements.description: Anti-ligature wall panels, demountable partition systems, and impact-resistant linings

elements.name: Bathroom pods
elements.description: Anti-ligature bathroom pods with concealed services, certified to DVA anti-ligature standards

elements.name: Mechanical services
elements.description: New HVAC installation with prefabricated ductwork sections and pre-assembled valve stations

elements.name: Electrical and security services
elements.description: New electrical distribution, anti-ligature lighting, nurse call system, and CCTV

items.name: BIM Level 2 or above
items.description: BIM Level 2 with point cloud survey of existing building informing design model

items.name: Digital twin strategy
items.description: Not in scope for this refurbishment project

items.name: Automated design-to-manufacture data exchange
items.description: Direct data exchange with bathroom pod manufacturer from Revit model

items.name: Platform approach to design for manufacture
items.description: Limited applicability due to existing building constraints; standardised within ward typology only

items.name: Use of golden thread for product tracking
items.description: Product tracking implemented for all anti-ligature components for Building Safety Act compliance

items.name: 3D laser scanning for as-built verification
items.description: Point cloud scanning used for existing building survey and installation verification
